dedupe_keys.name: resilio network of smart blue green roofs in amsterdam urban innovative actions

description: RESILIO (Resilience nEtwork of Smart Innovative cLImate-adapative rOoftops) built more than 10,000 square metres of smart blue-green roofs in Amsterdam, at least 8,000 on social housing, to store rainwater under the plant layer. Each roof has smart flow control with sensors and remote valves that retain or release water from weather forecasts and water management settings, and the roofs are linked in a network so water levels are regulated remotely, a new kind of real-time adaptive urban water management. The partners were the City of Amsterdam, Waternet, Hogeschool van Amsterdam, Vrije Universiteit, MetroPolder, three housing associations and Rooftop Revolution, with an ERDF grant of 4,814,248 euros; the project was completed in April 2022. Targets were 5,600 cubic metres of rainwater managed a year across four pilot neighbourhoods and 1,500 residents engaged; a project article describes assessing the roofs' hydraulic performance with 1D/2D urban flood models, such as Waternet's Infoworks ICM, against baseline and climate-changed storms. The UIA and project pages are accessible online as free HTML. Caveats: results are reported as meeting targets without published monitoring data. It illustrates real-time operation of green infrastructure for pluvial flood, heat and drought adaptation; related records are the Copenhagen cloudburst plan and Augustenborg stormwater case studies.
